memory_update.text: STRA should remain a reference/context asset for employer-funded higher education because public company materials explicitly disclose employer-partner and workforce-solutions positioning.

UTI is a high-relevance underfollowed candidate for employer-connected short-cycle certificates and technical-workforce bottlenecks; verify actual employer-funded revenue rather than assuming all industry partnerships are monetized.

FC is a small-cap underfollowed enterprise-training supplier; the thesis depends on recurring enterprise L&D demand and may fail if corporate training budgets remain weak or federal-contract headwinds persist.

Private university examples such as Bellevue University and University of Phoenix show the node is real, but public-market mapping is indirect; later layers should verify which public companies have durable employer-paid contracts rather than only employer marketing claims.

node: Employer-funded workforce training and short-cycle certificates
summary: Expanded the universe around employer-funded workforce training and short-cycle certificates with a two-lane funnel. Reference/context assets are mid-cap public education platforms with explicit career-learning or employer-partner language. The underfollowed discovery lane emphasizes employer-connected technical schools and enterprise training vendors where education exposure is hidden inside workforce development, technical-skills pipelines, leadership training, or HR/L&D budgets rather than consumer edtech. No buy/sell view is implied.
